Definition: to entrap (with a noose), literally or figuratively
BiblicalUsage: Naqash means to entrap with a noose, to lay a snare, and it is used for idolatry and for a king's trap. In 1 Samuel 28:9 the woman of Endor asks Saul why he lays a snare for her life, when he himself cut off those with familiar spirits, and in Deuteronomy 12:30 the people are warned not to be snared by following the gods of the nations after they are destroyed.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a snare is always set where you are already walking, because Saul finds his in the very place he once cleansed, and Israel is warned about the gods of the land they are about to enter; the way out of a snare is to see it before you step in it.
